behavioral_notes.observation: The modern external API surface. Path components map directly onto an ORM call: it resolves request.env[__model__].with_context(context) (NotFound if the model is absent), then get_public_method(Model, __method__) from odoo.service.model, which refuses any name starting with '_', any name in _UNSAFE_ATTRIBUTES, classmethods/staticmethods and methods decorated @api.private (raising AccessError/NotFound). It then Model.browse(ids), validates the call against inspect.signature(func).bind(records, **kwargs) (422 UnprocessableEntity on mismatch), rejects ids for @api.model methods (422), and calls func(records, **kwargs). A BaseModel recordset result is coerced to result.ids before serialization. There is no per-model/method allow-list: any public ORM method on any installed model is reachable - the security boundary is get_public_method plus normal ORM access rights, not the route.

Authentication is an API key, not a login session. The handler parses 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' (case-insensitive regex) and calls res.users.apikeys._check_credentials(scope='rpc', key=token); an invalid/absent key raises 401 Unauthorized with a WWWAuthenticate('bearer') challenge. The resolved uid drives request.update_env(user=uid) so the call runs with that user's rights. The endpoint is stateless: @route forces save_session=False for bearer routes and the handler sets request.session.can_save=False (no session cookie is written). With no bearer token it falls back to an existing session, but only when browser Sec-Fetch-* headers prove an interactive same-origin navigation (CSRF protection); otherwise it rejects. This auth-mode wiring is entirely invisible to ORM/model metadata.

Defines the request/response contract for /json/2. The body must be application/json (or empty); it is parsed via request.get_json_data() and merged with the URL path args into request.params (BadRequest on malformed JSON). A successful controller return is wrapped with request.make_json_response(result) - a bare JSON value, NOT a JSON-RPC {jsonrpc,id,result} envelope. handle_error serializes exceptions as JSON via serialize_exception with a meaningful HTTP status: UserError/SessionExpiredException use exc.http_status, werkzeug HTTPExceptions keep their .code (e.g. 404/422), everything else is 500. This REST-style JSON-over-HTTP envelope is the deliberate replacement for the legacy JSON-RPC framing.

Read/write routing is computed per request: _web_json_2_rpc_readonly walks Model.mro() for a method-level _readonly flag on the target method and returns it (default False), so read-only ORM methods dispatch to a read-replica cursor while write methods use the primary. A missing model short-circuits to readonly=True (a 404 needs no write cursor). The landing route /json/2 (and /json/2/<subpath>) is a deliberate 404 returning the hint 'Did you mean POST /json/2/<model>/<method>?' - there is no schema/OpenAPI discovery endpoint; the contract is simply 'any public method on any model'.

The historical endpoints. /jsonrpc and /xmlrpc/<service> dispatch via odoo.http.dispatch_rpc(service, method, params) over the common/db/object services, auth='none' (credentials travel in the call payload, not headers). xmlrpc_1 returns fault codes as strings (non-compliant, kept for back-compat) and xmlrpc_2 as ints (RPC_FAULT_CODE_* mapped from odoo.exceptions by xmlrpc_handle_exception_*). A custom OdooMarshaller serializes Odoo types (frozendict, bytes->base64 str, datetime/date->ISO strings, lazy, Markup, Command) and strips XML control characters. All three legacy routes log RPC_DEPRECATION_NOTICE (deprecated in 19, removal scheduled for 22) and call _check_request(), which closes the cursor (request.env.cr.close) before dispatch.

extract_frontend.py reports present=false: 0 JS files, 0 XML/QWeb templates, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 0 asset bundles. rpc ships no UI whatsoever - it is pure HTTP/RPC plumbing consumed by third-party clients and server-to-server callers, never rendered. The only 'discovery' surface is the unauthenticated GET /web/version (alias /json/version) returning {version_info, version} from odoo.release as a JSON response.

it_architecture.application: rpc (external programmatic API surface: JSON-2 REST-style API, legacy XML-RPC / JSON-RPC endpoints, version discovery)
logical_data_erm: rpc owns no models; it dispatches to any installed model via request.env[model]
bearer auth depends on res.users.apikeys (base) to resolve a token to a uid
information_flows: json2: third-party client -> POST /json/2/<model>/<method> (Bearer apikey) -> _auth_method_bearer -> get_public_method -> Model.browse(ids).<method>(**kwargs) -> JSON result
legacy: client -> /jsonrpc | /xmlrpc[/2]/<service> -> dispatch_rpc(service, method, params) -> common/db/object services
envelope: Json2Dispatcher.dispatch -> ir.http._dispatch -> make_json_response; handle_error -> serialize_exception with HTTP status

capabilities: Expose ORM Methods as an External Programmatic API (JSON-2)
Authenticate API Clients via Bearer API Keys
Enforce the Public-Method / Access-Right Security Boundary on Remote Calls
Serialize Odoo/ORM Types to Wire Formats (JSON, XML-RPC)
Advertise Server Version for Client Capability Negotiation
value_streams: Integration request-to-result: external client authenticates with an API key -> invokes a model method -> receives a JSON result (the integration round-trip)
policies: get_public_method gate: only non-underscore, non-@api.private, non-classmethod public methods are remotely callable; everything else raises AccessError
bearer auth required for /json/2/<model>/<method>; stateless (save_session=False, can_save=False), no session cookie
Sec-Fetch-* CSRF check when falling back from a bearer token to an interactive session
legacy /xmlrpc, /xmlrpc/2, /jsonrpc deprecated in 19.0, scheduled removal in 22.0 (RPC_DEPRECATION_NOTICE)
stakeholders: Third-party / external integration developer (primary consumer of /json/2 and legacy RPC)
System administrator (issues and scopes API keys via res.users.apikeys)

classification.rationale: rpc is firm IT infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'), not a value-creating primary activity of any chain/shop/network. It owns no business object: model_count=0, 0 fields, 0 security rules, 0 views, 0 frontend assets - only 6 routes / ~662 LOC of controllers that expose OTHER modules' ORM methods to external callers. It creates no value of its own; its value is enabling integration with whatever business modules are installed - the definition of a support/infrastructure surface. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' fits because rpc is the IT-delivery capability for external application interfaces ('develop and manage IT services / external integration interfaces / APIs'), the programmatic-access plumbing the firm's IT operates. 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' was considered (an API is an enabling capability others build on) but rejected: rpc is a concrete running interface/runtime, not a governance/portfolio capability - its work is IT service delivery (operate the API gateway, manage credentials, maintain protocol compatibility), squarely APQC 8.0, mirroring the web framework module's classification.

standard_capabilities: JSON-2 REST-style external API: POST /json/2/<model>/<method> to any public ORM method
Automatic ORM type serialization to JSON (json2) and XML-RPC (OdooMarshaller)
Backwards-compatible XML-RPC (/xmlrpc, /xmlrpc/2) and JSON-RPC (/jsonrpc) over common/db/object services
Structured JSON error envelopes with correct HTTP status (404/422/500)
typical_fits: External system reads/writes Odoo records via search_read / create / write over /json/2 with an API key
Legacy client kept working on /xmlrpc/2 until migration to /json/2
Server-to-server automation invoking action_* / business methods remotely
common_gaps: No schema/OpenAPI discovery endpoint - clients must know model/method names out of band
No per-route allow-list or rate limiting (any public method on any model is reachable; security is ORM access rights only)
API keys are global-scope ('rpc' scope maps to a NULL/global key) - no fine-grained per-endpoint scoping
Webhook / outbound push integration is not provided here - rpc is inbound/pull only
Legacy XML-RPC/JSON-RPC removal in 22.0 forces migration of older clients

open_questions: Exact wire shape clients send to /json/2: how positional ids vs kwargs are split for non-@api.model methods (the controller binds signature(func).bind(records, **kwargs); only ids + kwargs are top-level params).
Whether any deployment fronts /json/2 with a route allow-list or gateway rate limiting (not in this module).
Real-world API-key scoping practice - the 'rpc' scope maps to a global NULL-scope key; how installations restrict that.
Adoption split between legacy /xmlrpc(/2) + /jsonrpc and the new /json/2 ahead of the 22.0 removal.
